papers.title: The circadian system is affected by Alzheimers disease independently from amyloid beta deposits
papers.summary: The study investigated circadian disruption in APP/PS1 mice, finding reduced REM sleep, altered body temperature rhythms, hyperactivity of melanopsin-expressing retinal ganglion cells at young age and hypoactivity at older ages, and changes in SCN connectomics and gene expression without amyloid plaques in the ventral hypothalamus. These findings suggest AD affects the circadian system independently of amyloid-beta deposits.

papers.title: SEDAT: A hybrid tokenizer for large EEG models.
papers.summary: The paper introduces SEDAT, a hybrid tokenizer for EEG foundation models that combines spatial aggregation, signal decomposition, adaptive segmentation, and frequency-domain resampling. Evaluated on 10 diverse EEG datasets with four large models, SEDAT improves classification accuracy by up to 15.3% over fixed-length windowing and shows better feature separability, with lower computational complexity.

papers.title: Influence of Surgical-Level Propofol Anesthesia on Non-Rapid Eye Movement and Rapid Eye Movement Sleep in Aged Mice.
papers.summary: The study examined the effects of surgical-level propofol anesthesia on sleep in aged mice. Results showed increased wakefulness, decreased NREM and REM sleep, and a delayed REM rebound after emergence, indicating that propofol anesthesia differentially affects NREM and REM sleep and alters REM regulation in aged animals.

papers.title: The mTOR pathway drives daily physiology
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that mTOR is a major clock output pathway required for most daily variation in mammalian physiology, with PERIOD2 interacting directly with mTORC1. Acute mTOR inhibition abolishes functional rhythms in cells and most daily liver physiology, while preserving sleep/wake cycles, and shows evolutionary conservation as a circadian effector across species.

papers.title: Modulation of rapid eye movement sleep deprivation via transcranial ultrasound stimulation of the basal forebrain in mice.
papers.summary: This study evaluated the effects of transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) of the basal forebrain on sleep-deprived mice. TUS significantly increased REM sleep, enhanced delta and theta power, improved cognitive performance, restored hippocampal neuronal counts, and elevated serum cortisol levels, suggesting a potential non-pharmacological strategy for mitigating sleep insufficiency.

papers.title: Transcriptome and proteome associated to the sex-dependent effects of Neuroligin-2 absence on wakefulness and sleep features
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of Neuroligin-2 (NLGN2) absence on sleep/wake phenotypes and cortical omic profiles in male and female mice. They found sex-dependent changes in sleep architecture and electrocorticographic activity, with less than 31% of transcriptomic and 15% of proteomic changes shared between sexes, indicating that NLGN2 effects on sleep and molecular landscapes differ by biological sex.

papers.title: Sleep Bursts of Cranial Forces- a Potential Marker of Neurodegenerative Disease
papers.summary: This paper identifies a novel phenomenon called Sleep Bursts (SBs), brief periodic bursts in cranial forces during sleep, characterized in healthy subjects and those with neurodegenerative disease (NDD). SBs occurred at lower rates in NDD subjects, with reduced EEG delta power, suggesting a potential marker for neurodegenerative disease and a possible link to glymphatic drainage.

papers.title: Chronic trazodone treatment consolidates sleep, improves memory, and reduces amyloid pathology in a mouse model of Alzheimers disease
papers.summary: Chronic trazodone treatment in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease consolidates sleep, improves memory, and reduces amyloid pathology, including a 45% reduction in hippocampal plaque burden in aged mice.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Dynamics Across Sleep Stages in Alzheimer's Disease: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This pilot study examined EEG microstate dynamics across sleep stages in Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients versus healthy controls, finding significant alterations in microstate parameters and transition probabilities, particularly during wakefulness. These changes correlated with MMSE scores, suggesting sleep-stage-resolved microstate analysis as a potential tool for assessing AD.

papers.title: EEG Microstates and Related Brain Networks During Light Sleep.
papers.summary: This study used simultaneous EEG-fMRI during light sleep (N1 and N2) to relate EEG microstates to brain networks, finding Microstate C associated with cerebellum and Microstate D with thalamus and motor areas. The results highlight distinct network relationships between N1 and N2 sleep and implicate thalamus and motor cortex as key substrates.

papers.title: Mating imperatives drive plasticity of the daily temporal niche in fruit flies.
papers.summary: This study shows that intense sociosexual interactions rapidly reshape the crepuscular activity niche in fruit flies, with the direction of shift predicted by dominant sensory modality (chemosensation shifts to night, vision to day). This plasticity bypasses the circadian clock via a dopaminergic pathway, suggesting a mechanism for sympatric coexistence.

papers.title: Biological and Habitual Factors That Influence Sleep and Circadian Rhythm: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes biological and habitual factors influencing sleep and circadian rhythm, including gene haplotype, chronotype, gut microbiome, and modifiable variables like meal timing and physical activity. It identifies research gaps and suggests that manipulating these factors can improve sleep and circadian alignment.

papers.title: EEG microstate reconfiguration across cognitive states in preschool children with developmental language disorder.
papers.summary: This study examined EEG microstate organization in preschool children with developmental language disorder (DLD) versus typically developing peers across three cognitive tasks. Findings show microstate features vary by task context, but no robust DLD-specific alterations were found, suggesting limited evidence for microstate changes in this sample.

papers.title: A unified foundation model for heterogeneous EEG signal modeling via language-aligned semi-supervised learning.
papers.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
papers.summary: The paper introduces USEA, a unified semi-supervised EEG-language alignment framework for heterogeneous EEG data, using a single backbone with autoregressive reconstruction and label semantic embedding. It achieves competitive performance on nine public datasets, demonstrating scalability and effectiveness for EEG foundation modeling.

papers.title: The ups and downs of heart rate during sleep: a source of heterogeneity in individuals with obstructive sleep apnoea.
papers.summary: This study analyzed heart rate (HR) distributions during sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) versus non-SDB periods in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). It identified four chronotropic response patterns (bradycardic, tachycardic, mixed, neither), with bradycardic patients showing more severe apnea and higher hypoxic burden, highlighting heterogeneity in autonomic responses.

papers.title: Multi-modal sleep staging in the clinic for REM sleep behaviour disorder
papers.summary: This study compared single-channel EEG deep learning and multimodal feature-based models for sleep staging in REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD), finding that multimodal integration and cohort-specific training improve performance, especially for REM staging. Attention analysis highlighted EEG dominance and EOG contribution during REM, leading to a reduced-channel configuration that matched or improved performance.

papers.title: Metabolic collapse as a mechanism of developmental regression: convergent evidence from Kleefstra syndrome FDG-PET/CT imaging and Drosophila modelling
papers.summary: This study investigated metabolic alterations in Kleefstra syndrome (KLEFS1) using FDG-PET/CT and Drosophila models, finding hypometabolism in regressed individuals and increased metabolic rate with sleep fragmentation in mutants. Oxidative stress worsened sleep and reduced metabolic output, but high sugar feeding prevented these effects, suggesting metabolic vulnerability underlies regression.

papers.title: Integrating Spatial-Temporal Channel Reliability with AI for Robust High-Frequency Oscillation Detection in Intracranial EEG.
papers.journal: International IEEE/EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering : [proceedings]. International IEEE EMBS Conference on Neural Engineering
papers.summary: The authors developed a reliability-guided HFO detection pipeline incorporating event-level denoising, channel signal quality assessment, and segment-level temporal reliability analysis. Applied to iEEG data, the pipeline improved SOZ localization accuracy from 66% baseline to 93% after filtering, enhancing clinical specificity.

papers.title: ViSTA-SleepNet: A View-Integrated and Subject-Adaptive Transformer Framework for Multimodal Sleep Staging.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The paper introduces ViSTA-SleepNet, a two-stage multi-view multimodal transformer framework for sleep staging that integrates EEG, EOG, and EMG signals with demographic information. It achieved accuracies of 88.5%, 84.5%, and 89.6% on Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78, and SHHS datasets respectively, with over 95% accuracy in spindle and slow-wave detection.

papers.title: Sleep disorders and executive-function inefficiency in boys with intellectual disabilities: A cross-sectional comparative study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared sleep symptoms and executive functions in boys with intellectual disabilities (ID) versus typically developing controls. Boys with ID had significantly higher sleep-disorder scores and poorer executive function, and within the ID group, higher sleep scores correlated with worse working memory, planning, inhibition, and attention.

papers.title: Non-Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Instability in Children With Epilepsy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Cyclic Alternating Patterns.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed cyclic alternating pattern (CAP) parameters in children with epilepsy versus healthy controls. Pooled analysis found no significant difference in total CAP rate, but the A3 index was lower in epilepsy, though not robust in sensitivity analyses, indicating heterogeneous, syndrome-specific alterations.

papers.title: Association Between Alzheimer Pathology, Sleep, and Cognition in Patients With Late-Onset Unexplained Epilepsy.
papers.summary: In patients with late-onset unexplained epilepsy (LOUE), higher plasma p-tau217 levels were associated with poorer cognition and reduced spindle-slow oscillation coupling. Mediation analysis suggested that spindle-SO coupling accounted for ~24% of the p-tau217-cognition association, supporting p-tau217 as a biomarker and highlighting sleep's role.

papers.title: Differences in circadian rhythm changes between myopic and non-myopic college students over 2 years.
papers.summary: This 2-year cohort study of college students found that myopic students had later bedtimes, earlier wake-up times, and lower chronotype scores at baseline. Over follow-up, only myopic students showed a 45-minute delay in dim-light melatonin onset, indicating significant circadian rhythm changes in myopia.

papers.title: Sleep Quality, Daytime Sleepiness, and Circadian Rhythm Characteristics in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study Across Disease Stages.
papers.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 344 adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD) found that dialysis-dependent patients had significantly higher daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale) but paradoxically lower global subjective sleep quality (PSQI) scores compared to earlier stages. Daytime sleepiness and dialysis status were the only significant predictors of PSQI global scores.

papers.title: Large-scale EEG neural network changes following accelerated high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation in major depressive disorder: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial, 39 MDD patients received either medication alone or medication plus accelerated HD-tDCS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. The HD-tDCS group showed greater reductions in depression scores and significant EEG microstate changes, with decreased coverage of microstates A and D and increased coverage of B, correlating with symptom improvement.

papers.title: Integrating socioeconomic context with multimodal EEG data for improved ADHD risk screening.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a multimodal deep learning model that combines EEG signals and socioeconomic context to screen for ADHD risk. The model outperformed EEG-only baselines in epoch-level cross-validation, achieving accuracy improvements of 2.1-5.9% and sensitivity gains up to 12.2%, but subject-independent results were more modest, suggesting it is a proof-of-concept.

papers.title: Dynamic Global and Local Enhancement of Theta-Band Functional Networks as Neural Markers of Spinal Cord Stimulation Efficacy in Disorders of Consciousness.
papers.summary: In 19 patients with disorders of consciousness undergoing 70 Hz spinal cord stimulation (SCS), responders showed enhanced global integration and decoupled regional segregation in theta-band dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) compared to non-responders. These dFC changes correlated with 3-month clinical improvement, suggesting a neural marker for SCS efficacy.

papers.title: Impaired midfrontal‑motor theta phase synchronization characterizes maladaptive motivational behavior in people with obsessive‑compulsive disorder.
papers.summary: This study used a motivational Go/NoGo learning task with EEG to examine maladaptive biases in OCD. People with OCD showed stronger Pavlovian bias and lower learning rates, and while they displayed increased midfrontal theta power related to conflict detection, midfrontal-motor theta phase synchrony was not enhanced and failed to modulate these biases, revealing a neural mechanism for the insight-action dissociation.

papers.title: Childhood maltreatment, circadian preference, and hs-CRP in first-episode, drug-naïve major depressive disorder: total- and symptom-level associations.
papers.summary: In 133 first-episode drug-naïve MDD patients, childhood maltreatment was associated with both self-reported and clinician-rated depression severity, while eveningness was associated with self-reported severity, particularly sleep problems. hs-CRP showed no independent association with depressive severity after adjusting for BMI.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Weekend Catch-Up Sleep and Hypertension: Insights From the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, 2017-2023.
papers.summary: An analysis of NHANES 2017-2023 data (16,268 adults) found no robust association between weekend catch-up sleep duration and hypertension, with only the 0-1 hour category showing lower odds compared to no catch-up sleep, and no dose-response relationship.

papers.title: Sleep Deprivation, Cytokine Dysregulation, and the Risk of Cardiac Arrhythmia in Dogs.
papers.summary: This systematic review and network analysis found that sleep deprivation in dogs is associated with a coordinated inflammatory response involving cytokines such as IL-6, TNF, and CRP, which may converge on pathways that increase arrhythmia susceptibility.

papers.title: Prenatal road traffic noise impairs early testicular development in Sprague-Dawley offspring: pharmacological rescue by melatonin and edaravone; developmental preservation by environmental enrichment.
papers.summary: This study exposed pregnant rats to road traffic noise and found reduced testicular development in male offspring, including lower organ weights, testosterone, and antioxidant enzymes, plus increased oxidative stress and inflammation. Combined melatonin and edaravone treatment or environmental enrichment restored normal development, identifying RTN as a modifiable risk factor and suggesting pharmacological rescue strategies.

papers.title: Association of sleep duration, lifestyle habits, and motor vehicle accident mortality-A prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 482,507 adults, both short (<6 hours) and long (>8 hours) sleep durations were associated with a ~30% increased risk of motor vehicle accident mortality, with risks amplified among smokers, frequent alcohol drinkers, and sleeping pill users.

papers.title: Electroencephalography-Based Measures to Understand Meditation and Mindfulness: Bibliometric Scoping Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.journal: Global advances in integrative medicine and health
papers.summary: This bibliometric scoping review mapped randomized controlled trials (RCTs) using EEG-based measures for meditation and mindfulness-based interventions, identifying 142 eligible publications from 31 countries. Significant heterogeneity was found in study populations, experimental designs, and outcomes, indicating that further systematic reviews require more original studies.

papers.title: Nigro-striatal deficits capture phenoconversion risk in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder
papers.summary: This prospective study of 56 iRBD patients over 11 years found that phenoconversion risk was associated with reduced putamen dopamine transporter binding (HR=3.1), SN neuromelanin loss (HR=2.5), SN free water (HR=1.54), and LC/LsC neuromelanin loss (HR=2.1). SN and LC/LsC neuromelanin contributed independently, suggesting that NM-MRI could be an alternative to nuclear imaging for estimating phenoconversion risk.

papers.title: Sleepiness and Clinical Readiness in Prelicensure Undergraduate Nursing Students.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 83 nursing students found that higher sleepiness (KSS) was associated with higher PSQI scores, and only medication administration skills checkoff showed a significant difference by sleepiness group (U=338, P=.016). Other skills and logistic regression models were nonsignificant, though descriptive trends suggested possible links between sleepiness and performance.

papers.title: Does daylight saving time increase traffic crashes? Seasonal confounding and a morning fatality effect.
papers.summary: Using a difference-in-differences design with non-DST states as controls, this study found no significant overall increase in fatal crashes after DST transitions (0.2%, p=0.954), but morning (6-10 AM) fatal crashes increased by 25.9% (p=0.007) after spring-forward. The findings suggest previous uncontrolled comparisons may overstate DST's overall crash effect, while highlighting a targeted morning fatality increase.

papers.title: Sleep Duration and Quality, Sleep Disorders and Their Association with Adiposity Markers in Adults from the Middle East: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluated associations between sleep duration, quality, disorders and adiposity markers in Middle Eastern and North African adults. It found that short sleep and obstructive sleep apnea were associated with higher adiposity, but insomnia showed no significant link, and sex-specific associations remain uncertain.

papers.title: Acute total sleep deprivation transiently increases plasma total tau but not plasma P-tau181 in healthy adults.
papers.summary: In this exploratory study, 20 healthy adults underwent 24h total sleep deprivation followed by recovery sleep. Plasma total tau increased by 35% after sleep deprivation and decreased by 38% after recovery, while plasma P-tau181 showed no significant changes, suggesting short-term sleep loss affects nonspecific neuronal markers.

papers.title: Prevalence, characteristics, and determinants of chest pain among physicians in the Middle East and North Africa: A multinational cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This multinational cross-sectional study of 6,224 physicians in 12 MENA countries found that 12.8% had definitive anginal pain and 45.6% had possible anginal pain. Panic disorder was the strongest predictor, followed by physical comorbidities, sleep deprivation, female sex, anxiety, obesity, and nicotine use.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
